title: Quarterly sprint: commitment-decoupling for dedicated pools + autoscale simulation labs
creator: Ayesha Khan
description:
Problem statement: Customers with dedicated reservations frequently over-commit for peak windows which increases unit cost. Current autoscale behavior is tightly coupled to reservation windows and per-pool policies, making it hard for product teams to buy less committed capacity while preserving latency SLOs.

Objective: In Q1 we will run a focused sprint to decouple long-term reservation commitments from short-term responsiveness by building a lightweight virtual pool overlay and an autoscale simulation lab. This initiative targets a 10–20% reduction in committed spend for pilot customers while maintaining p99 latency within 1.2x of baseline.

Scope:
- Design an API-level abstraction (Virtual Pool Overlay) that lets customers route a subset of traffic to a responsive autoscale overlay without changing their reservation contract.
- Implement guardrails and cost-visibility controls in Console for VPO routing (per-route budget caps, prewarm caps, and soft-fallback thresholds).
- Build an autoscale Simulation Lab: a reproducible harness that replays anonymized production traces, exercises burst scenarios, and outputs cost/latency trade-off reports.
- Canary rollout: run VPO + autoscale simulations for 3 pilot customers, capture real workload runs, and iterate on policy thresholds.

Success metrics: 1) pilot customers reduce reserved capacity commitment by >= 10% without exceeding p99 SLA by >20% during the pilot; 2) autoscale simulation lab provides stable cost/latency deltas within a 5% margin vs live canary results; 3) Console shows per-route projection and a “recommended commitment” number for customers in the pilot.
acceptance_criteria: VPO API spec merged and reviewed in Confluence (link in notes)
Autoscale Simulation Lab can replay 7 days of anonymized production traces and produce cost/latency delta reports
Console UI: per-route overlay toggle, projected cost delta, and soft-fallback policy exposed to pilot customers
Canary run completed with three pilot customers showing >=10% reduction in reserved commit for at least one month window without p99 breach >1.2x baseline
Runbook drafted for on-call escalation when VPO fallback triggers more than 3 times in 24 hours

notes: 2026-01-14 — Design review: agreed to keep VPO as a non-billable overlay initially to avoid billing churn. Action: PM to add telemetry events for routing decisions (Liam).

2026-01-28 — Spike results: Simulation Lab replay showed a median cost reduction of 18% but a 7% increase in p99 for one heavy-tail workload (reason: cache warmup delays). Eng proposed a prefix-KV prewarm optimization for the overlay route.

2026-02-03 — Security review kickoff: Legal and Security confirmed no new data residency issues for anonymized traces. Security requested an HMAC-signature for exported trace bundles (ticket ENG-6123).
2026-02-20 — PM/Design feedback: Console projection needs clearer uncertainty bands; defer final copy until design round 2. Design owner: Sofia Martinez.

2026-02-27 — Canary readiness: feature flag toggle and canary checklist completed. Ops to monitor cost deltas and p99; alert thresholds set in PagerDuty (link to runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEDICATED/VPO+Runbook).

2026-03-01 — Interim analysis: First 48h of pilot for customer A shows 12% reserved commit reduction and p99 at 1.08x baseline. Customer B showed noisier metrics — Eng to run targeted KV prewarm for B's workload (ENG-7245).
